clue.text: Wonderful hospital leaving well-funded structure

parts.note: fab is informal for wonderful

indicators.note: the hospital letter leaving the word means it is taken out of it

parts.note: well-funded means rich

explanation.surface: A rich institution loses its hospital, though the clue sounds like praise for a building.
explanation.definitionFit: Fabric can mean the basic framework or physical makeup of a building or society, its structure.

clue.text: Plates holding British (English) loan certificates

indicators.note: holding means the first word's letters contain the others

parts.note: plates is a word for false teeth, dentures

explanation.surface: Something about plates and British loans, with a parenthetical aside about England.
explanation.definitionFit: Debentures are bonds issued by a company acknowledging a long-term loan, so they are certificates of debt.

clue.text: Beer enthusiasts about to drink a good new brandy

indicators.note: to drink means to take the following letters inside
about signals that the beer group's letters turn round

parts.note: CAMRA is the Campaign for Real Ale, a British group of beer enthusiasts

explanation.surface: Real-ale fans about to switch to a fine new brandy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' turns CAMRA into ARMAC; 'to drink' puts A, G and N inside it. CAMRA (Campaign for Real Ale) is a British consumer group for traditional beer.
explanation.definitionFit: Armagnac is a grape brandy from the Gascony region of France, a named type of brandy.

clue.text: Narrow stripe in piece of meat round end of skewer

indicators.note: round means the meat's letters go around the next letter

parts.note: a steak is a piece of meat

indicators.note: end of means the last letter of skewer is taken

explanation.surface: A cook spots a thin line in a cut of meat near the tip of a skewer.
explanation.definitionFit: A streak is a long thin line or band of a different colour, a narrow stripe.

clue.text: Scene 10 rewritten as a punishment

indicators.note: rewritten means the letters are written out again in a new order

parts.note: 10 is ten in words

explanation.surface: A playwright is forced to redo the tenth scene as a penalty.
explanation.definitionFit: A sentence is the penalty a court hands down, a judicial punishment.

clue.text: Warning issued by Conservatives infiltrated by far-right movement

indicators.note: infiltrated by means the second piece gets inside the first

parts.note: conservatives collectively are the political right
the EDL, English Defence League, is a British far-right street movement

explanation.surface: A political warning that extremists have crept into the Tory party.
explanation.walkthrough: The EDL (English Defence League) is a British far-right protest group.
explanation.definitionFit: A red light is a stop signal, used figuratively for any warning or signal of danger.

clue.text: Country conserving head of prehistoric freshwater creature

indicators.note: conserving means holding a letter safely inside

parts.note: country in the sense of landscape or terrain

indicators.note: head of means the first letter of prehistoric

explanation.surface: A land that preserves an ancient freshwater animal, like a living fossil.
explanation.definitionFit: A terrapin is a small turtle that lives in fresh or brackish water.

clue.text: PM's meagre salary halved

indicators.note: halved means only the first half of the word is kept

parts.note: a pittance is a meagre wage

explanation.surface: A prime minister's poor pay is cut in half.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's after PM stands for 'is', linking definition and wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: Pitt the Elder and Pitt the Younger were both British prime ministers.

clue.text: Standard number assigned to soldiers

parts.note: RM, the Royal Marines, are soldiers serving with the navy

explanation.surface: A regulation number given to each soldier.
explanation.definitionFit: A norm is an accepted standard or usual level against which things are measured.

clue.text: Lowest points in faulty drains

indicators.note: faulty means the letters are out of order, wrongly arranged

explanation.surface: A plumber traces the worst spots in a broken drainage system.
explanation.definitionFit: A nadir is the lowest point of something, originally the point of the sky directly underfoot.

clue.text: 11, perhaps, fixed games with sailor

indicators.note: fixed games are rigged, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: tar is an old word for a sailor

explanation.surface: A rock guitarist accused of rigging matches with a seaman.
explanation.walkthrough: '11' points to the answer at 11 across, Eric Clapton; 'perhaps' marks him as an example.
explanation.definitionFit: Eric Clapton is a hugely famous performer, an instance of a megastar.

clue.text: Musician playing clarinet with cop

indicators.note: playing suggests the letters are played about with, set in a new order

explanation.surface: A musician performing on clarinet alongside a police officer.
explanation.definitionFit: Eric Clapton is a celebrated English rock and blues guitarist, a musician.

clue.text: Stake money on northbound Underground before departure

parts.note: an ante is a stake put up in poker

indicators.note: northbound in a down clue means the word reads upwards, so backwards

parts.note: a metro is an underground railway

explanation.surface: A gambler bets cash on the Tube heading north before leaving.
explanation.walkthrough: 'northbound' turns METRO into ORTEM, reading up the column.
explanation.definitionFit: Ante-mortem is Latin for before death, and departure is a euphemism for dying.

clue.text: Staff drowning feeble king in watercourse

indicators.note: drowning means the staff's letters close over the others, swallowing them

parts.note: a mace is a ceremonial staff
ill means unwell, feeble
R, for rex, is the abbreviation for king

explanation.surface: A rod holds a weak monarch under in a stream, a grim little drama.
explanation.definitionFit: A millrace is the channel carrying water to drive a mill wheel, a kind of watercourse.

clue.text: Ridiculous debates about base of solid frame in dormitory

indicators.note: about means the jumbled letters go around the next letter
ridiculous means the letters are absurdly jumbled
base of means the bottom, last, letter of solid

explanation.surface: Silly arguments over the foundations of a solid structure in a boarding school.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ridiculous' reworks DEBATES into BESTEAD; 'about' puts it around D from 'base of solid'.
explanation.definitionFit: A bedstead is the framework of a bed, the kind found lined up in a dormitory.

clue.text: Conservative and old Independent bath prepared to shack up together

indicators.note: prepared means the letters are made ready in a new arrangement

explanation.surface: A Tory and an old independent politician run a bath before moving in together.
explanation.walkthrough: 'prepared' rearranges I and BATH into HABIT.
explanation.definitionFit: To cohabit is to live together as partners without marrying, colloquially to shack up.

clue.text: Money found with stolen ammunition

parts.note: bucks are dollars, money
hot is slang for stolen goods

explanation.surface: Cash discovered alongside stolen bullets, like a crime scene inventory.
explanation.definitionFit: Buckshot is coarse lead shot fired from a shotgun, a type of ammunition.

clue.text: Record part of poem in lounge

parts.note: rec is a short form of record
a line is a part of a poem

explanation.surface: Recording a verse of poetry in a sitting room.
explanation.walkthrough: 'lounge' reads as a room, but it is the verb.
explanation.definitionFit: To lounge and to recline both mean to lie back in a relaxed way.

clue.text: Food arrives on recycled black tiles

parts.note: arrives means comes

indicators.note: recycled means the letters are reused in a new order

parts.note: B is the abbreviation for black, as on pencils

explanation.surface: Dinner turns up served on reclaimed dark tiles.
explanation.walkthrough: 'recycled' rearranges B and TILES into STIBLE.
explanation.definitionFit: Comestibles is a formal or humorous word for things to eat, food.

clue.text: Bring in setter's drink!

parts.note: setter's means the setter is, I'm
port is a fortified wine, a drink

explanation.surface: The setter cheerfully announces a fondness for fortified wine.
explanation.definitionFit: To import goods is to bring them in from abroad.

clue.text: Bottom of well covered by moist leather strip

indicators.note: covered by means the letter is enclosed by the other word

parts.note: moist means wet

indicators.note: bottom of in a down clue means the last letter of well

explanation.surface: The bottom of a well, damp and lined with leather.
explanation.definitionFit: A welt is a strip of leather joining a shoe's upper to its sole.

clue.text: Sporting fixture on river is level

parts.note: a tie is a sports match, as in a cup tie

explanation.surface: A match played on a river ends all square.
explanation.walkthrough: 'level' suggests a drawn score, but it is a noun.
explanation.definitionFit: A tier is one of several rows or layers set one above another, a level.

clue.text: Attention surrounding girl married to country's ultimate diplomat

indicators.note: surrounding means the first word goes around the second

parts.note: ear means attention, as in lend an ear
miss is a girl or young woman

indicators.note: ultimate means the last letter of country's

explanation.surface: A girl married to the country's top envoy commands attention.
explanation.definitionFit: An emissary is an envoy sent on a mission, a kind of diplomat.

clue.text: Drug setter took after surgery

indicators.note: after means the setter's piece follows the surgery

parts.note: op is short for operation, surgery
the setter refers to themself as I
ate means took food

explanation.surface: The setter took painkillers following an operation.
explanation.definitionFit: An opiate is a drug derived from opium, such as morphine.

clue.text: Money taken by business making a pastry dish

definitions.meaning: the total revenue a business takes in

explanation.surface: A firm earns its takings by baking pastries.
explanation.definitionFit: Turnover means a company's gross takings, and also a folded filled pastry.

clue.text: Female diner rearranged china

definitions.note: china, from china plate, is rhyming slang for mate

indicators.note: rearranged means the letters are put in a different order

explanation.surface: A woman eating out rearranges the crockery.
explanation.walkthrough: China is Cockney rhyming slang: china plate rhymes with mate, a friend.
explanation.definitionFit: In rhyming slang a china is a mate, someone you are close to.
